solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Dangerous reptile flusters hack regularly visiting north-east (11)

indicators.note: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is taken
a visitor goes inside someone's place, so these letters go inside the compass points

blocks.note: to rattle someone = to fluster them
second and fourth letters of hAcK

annotation.surface: A deadly snake sends a hacker into a flap somewhere in the north-east.
annotation.walkthrough: North-east reads as one region; it is split into its two compass letters so that AK can sit between them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: the rattlesnake is a venomous American viper.

entries.clue: Defiant chap entering further exam (9)

indicators.note: to enter is to go into a place, so the chap goes inside the exam word

blocks.note: a resit is an exam taken again

annotation.surface: A rebellious young man turns up to sit his exam again.
annotation.walkthrough: Crosswords use any short man's name for 'chap'; here it has to be one that fits inside the exam.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone who will not give way.

entries.clue: European citizen making cuts in opera? (3,6,2,7)

definitions.text: European citizen making cuts in opera?

blocks.note: a Spaniard, specifically a resident of a city in Andalusia
the man's trade is cutting hair
he is the title character of a Rossini comic opera

annotation.surface: Someone from Europe is trimming an opera down to size.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Making cuts in opera' reads as editing a score; the cuts are haircuts, and the opera is the title. There is no separate wordplay: the whole clue describes Figaro.
annotation.definitionFit: Figaro, the title character of Rossini's opera, is a barber living in Seville.

entries.clue: Turner’s device Henry invested in tardily (5)

indicators.note: to invest someone is to clothe them in robes, so Henry is wrapped in the word for tardily

blocks.note: to arrive tardily is to arrive late
H = henry, the unit of inductance

annotation.surface: A painter's apparatus in which a Henry has belatedly invested.
annotation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter J M W Turner; here it is a woodturner.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: a turner shapes wood or metal by spinning it on this machine.

entries.clue: He’s pressed hard, surprisingly, to find an animal minder (11)

indicators.note: the letters come out in an unexpected order

annotation.surface: A man under heavy pressure, oddly, turns out to look after animals.
annotation.walkthrough: 'He' sets up a man, and the answer is a woman.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: she minds a flock of sheep.

entries.clue: Rival church leader’s hint in article? Not at all (8)

indicators.note: in places the hint inside the word for 'Not at all'

annotation.surface: A question about whether a hint lies in an article about a rival church leader, answered with a flat no.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark fakes a question; 'Not at all' is just the slangy no, which follows the article and swallows the hint.
annotation.definitionFit: A historical term: a rival claimant to the papacy, set up against the elected pope.

entries.clue: Additional time welcomed by girl left outside union (12)

indicators.note: a guest welcomed by a host is taken in, so the girl's name takes the time letter inside

annotation.surface: A girl is left out of a trade union but welcomed for some extra time.
annotation.walkthrough: Union reads as a trade union; it is the union of marriage.
annotation.definitionFit: Marriage is a union, and the Latin extra means outside, so this is a literal gloss.

entries.clue: Old friend talked of spirit’s shimmering effect (11)

indicators.note: what is talked of is spoken, so the word for spirit is taken by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: essence = spirit, the core nature of a thing

annotation.surface: An old friend describes the shimmer of a ghost.
annotation.walkthrough: Spirit suggests a ghost or a drink; it means essence, the heart of a thing.
annotation.definitionFit: Named from the gem: the milky, shifting sheen of an opal.

entries.clue: Walk across street, supporting deliveries on cycle, perhaps? (10)

indicators.note: a support holds something up from below, and in a down answer the street sits under the deliveries

blocks.note: in cricket a set of six deliveries (balls) from one bowler
what you have on a bicycle

annotation.surface: A pedestrian crosses a street while someone delivers on a bike.
annotation.walkthrough: Deliveries looks like parcels on a bike; it is cricket, where a bowler's six balls make one unit of play.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal compound: to stride over, so to cross on foot.

entries.clue: Tree some vandal deracinated (5)

indicators.note: some of means only part of, so the answer is a run of letters from the words that follow

blocks.note: the end of vandal and the start of deracinated

annotation.surface: A vandal has pulled up a tree by its roots.
annotation.walkthrough: Deracinated means uprooted, which suits the tree but is only a hiding place.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a waterside tree of the birch family.

entries.clue: Soldier in outskirts of Epsom, overtaken and surrounded (11)

indicators.note: in places the soldier inside the town's edge letters
a town's outskirts are its edges, so only the first and last letters are used

blocks.note: first and last letters of EpsoM
a car that is overtaken has been passed

annotation.surface: A soldier on the edge of Epsom, a Surrey town, is passed by traffic and hemmed in.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a traffic scene; overtaken is a separate piece, not a description of the soldier.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be encompassed is to be enclosed on all sides.

entries.clue: Dry clinic oddly shaped like a tube (9)

indicators.note: arranged oddly means put in a strange order, so the letters are shuffled

annotation.surface: A teetotal clinic has been built in the shape of a tube.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' often means take the odd letters; here it simply means rearranged, and the fodder is exactly nine letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A geometric description: a tube is a hollow cylinder, and -ic makes the adjective.

entries.clue: Memo causing upset to college (4)

indicators.note: to upset is to knock over, and in a down answer the word is turned upside down

blocks.note: Eton, the English public school near Windsor

annotation.surface: A memo has caused a stir at a college.
annotation.walkthrough: Eton is the crossword's usual college.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a short written message.

entries.clue: Seamstress beheaded in jug? (4)

indicators.note: losing the head means losing the first letter

annotation.surface: A seamstress has been beheaded in jail.
annotation.walkthrough: Jug is slang for prison, which gives the grisly surface; the question mark flags that the jug here is the pitcher kind.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a large wide-mouthed jug, once used with a washbasin.

entries.clue: Last of kids shut up, being exhausted! (5)

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

annotation.surface: A parent finally gets the kids to shut up and collapses.
annotation.walkthrough: Shut up reads as a demand for quiet; it means confined, as in pent-up.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as a spent force or a spent runner.

entries.clue: Limited object the French authorise (7)

indicators.note: something limited is cut short, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: an entity is a thing, an object

annotation.surface: A limited company objects to what the French authorities sanction.
annotation.walkthrough: Limited suggests a company; it only tells you to trim the word after it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to give someone the right to do something.

entries.clue: Month a boxer initially talked about a liquid measure (9)

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is taken

annotation.surface: A boxer spent a month talking about how much liquid he drank.
annotation.walkthrough: Ali is the crossword's standard boxer, and 'a boxer' is one piece, not A plus a boxer.
annotation.definitionFit: A metric unit of volume: deca- means ten, so it is ten litres.

entries.clue: Interplanetary craft ultimately needs steps with it (9)

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is taken

annotation.surface: A spacecraft ends up needing boarding steps to be fashionable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With it' looks like a link meaning 'as well'; it is slang for trendy.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: a vehicle for travel between planets.

entries.clue: A singular type intended to dispose of a potpourri (10)

indicators.note: to dispose of something is to get rid of it, so the A is thrown out of the word for intended

blocks.note: the A taken out of MEANT

annotation.surface: An odd sort of person set out to get rid of a bowl of dried petals.
annotation.walkthrough: Singular looks like 'odd'; it is the grammar label, abbreviated S.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a potpourri is a medley or miscellany, from the mixed petals of the original.

entries.clue: Old king’s turbulent son faced sword there (6,3,9)

definitions.note: the definition carries the surface's possessive ('s = is); the answer is the king himself

indicators.note: turbulent means in violent disorder, so the letters are thrown about

annotation.surface: An old king's rebellious son has a sword drawn against him.
annotation.walkthrough: A long anagram in a scene of royal violence; the king in question was famously pious rather than warlike.
annotation.definitionFit: Edward the Confessor was an Anglo-Saxon king of England from 1042 to 1066.

entries.clue: Cable English member absorbed in public vehicle (8)

indicators.note: something absorbed in another is taken inside it, so the English member goes inside the vehicle

blocks.note: a tram is a public transport vehicle
a limb is a member of the body

annotation.surface: An electric cable runs through a tram, where an English passenger's leg is caught.
annotation.walkthrough: Cable is the wire in the surface; in older usage it is also a message sent by undersea cable.
annotation.definitionFit: An older sense: a cable was a telegram sent abroad by submarine cable.

entries.clue: Vicious dog accompanying a Republican judge (7)

indicators.note: to accompany is to go along with, so the dog is placed next to the other pieces

annotation.surface: A Republican judge arrives with a savage dog at his side.
annotation.walkthrough: The dog comes first in the clue but last in the answer; accompanying only says the pieces go together.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who settles a dispute.

entries.clue: Fairly lofty Tudor composer overcoming height (7)

indicators.note: to overcome is literally to come over, and in a down answer the composer sits above the height letter

blocks.note: Thomas Tallis, composer to the Tudor court

annotation.surface: A Tudor composer rises above his difficulties to reach a lofty height.
annotation.walkthrough: Byrd is the other Tudor composer crosswords use; only one of them starts with a word for lofty.
annotation.definitionFit: The -ish suffix means fairly, and tall means lofty.

entries.clue: Extremely popular breezy-sounding plain (7)

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the first and last letters are used
sounding like means heard rather than seen, so the word for breezy is taken by its sound

blocks.note: first and last letters of PopulaR

annotation.surface: A plain that is very popular for its fresh breeze.
annotation.walkthrough: Plain looks like an adjective meaning simple; it is a noun, flat grassland.
annotation.definitionFit: A geographical term: the vast grassy plains of North America.

entries.clue: Cheap informal English comedian entertaining small number (8)

definitions.note: informal is a dictionary label: using economic to mean cheap is colloquial

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them in, so the comedian holds the small number inside

blocks.note: no. is the short form of number

annotation.surface: A cheap English comic plays to a tiny audience.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Informal' belongs with Cheap, like a dictionary label, not with the comedian.
annotation.definitionFit: A colloquial sense: something economic gives good value, so it is cheap.

entries.clue: A newlywed taking in garments at first to shorten (7)

indicators.note: a tailor taking in a dress makes it smaller; here the newlywed takes a letter inside
at first means at the start, so only the first letter is taken

blocks.note: a woman who has just married

annotation.surface: A new bride takes in her dresses to make them shorter.
annotation.walkthrough: Taking in garments is dressmaking, and it even suits shortening; the wordplay only wants one letter taken in.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to abridge a book is to cut it down.

entries.clue: Trio mostly raving originally about sick suspense story (8)

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
originally means at the origin, the start, so only the first letter is taken
about means around, so these letters go round the word for sick

blocks.note: a trio is three, less its last letter

annotation.surface: Three people, raving mad, discuss a sick tale of suspense.
annotation.walkthrough: The container goes round a split point inside the shortened trio, not neatly around its ends.
annotation.definitionFit: A genre name: a novel or film built on suspense and excitement.

entries.clue: Disclose how age impaired a futile mission (4-5,5)

indicators.note: something impaired is damaged, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone is asked to reveal how getting old has weakened them, a pointless task.
annotation.walkthrough: Disclose looks like the instruction to reveal something hidden; it is only letters for the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a hopeless pursuit of something that cannot be caught.

entries.clue: Hospital doctor principally employing this form of communication (8)

indicators.note: principally means first and foremost, so the first letters are taken

blocks.note: an intern is a junior hospital doctor

annotation.surface: A hospital doctor mainly uses this way of getting in touch.
annotation.walkthrough: Intern is the American term for a junior doctor in training.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the worldwide computer network is a medium for messages.

entries.clue: Muslim legal expert’s everyday clothing (5)

blocks.note: a scholar who issues rulings on Islamic law
civilian clothes worn by someone who normally wears uniform

annotation.surface: A question of what an Islamic jurist wears day to day.
annotation.walkthrough: Wearing plain clothes is British usage, chiefly of soldiers or schoolchildren out of uniform.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are one word: the jurist's title, and the plain dress said to come from his image on the stage.

entries.clue: Note gun covering Tyler’s power unit (8)

indicators.note: a cover goes over and around something, so the gun wraps round Tyler's name

blocks.note: me (or mi), the third note of the sol-fa scale
Wat Tyler led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381

annotation.surface: A gunman keeps Tyler covered as he reaches for his power supply.
annotation.walkthrough: Tyler's first name is wanted: Wat Tyler, leader of the English Peasants' Revolt.
annotation.definitionFit: A metric unit: a million watts, used for power stations.

entries.clue: Unusually nasty adverse mark for use of language (6)

indicators.note: unusually means not in the usual way, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: a cross, the mark for a wrong answer

annotation.surface: A teacher's unusually harsh cross against a pupil's use of English.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram stops at nasty; the cross is added on after it.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose gloss: syntax is the way words are arranged, one aspect of how language is used.

entries.clue: Hardy character’s suitor carrying light by day (10)

indicators.note: to carry is to hold, so the suitor holds the other pieces inside
by means next to, so the day letter sits beside the word for light

blocks.note: to light on = to land on, alight

annotation.surface: A suitor in a Thomas Hardy novel carries a lamp by day.
annotation.walkthrough: Light is a verb, as a bird lights on a branch; the novel is Hardy's The Woodlanders.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Thomas Hardy's novel The Woodlanders is about people of a Dorset wood.

entries.clue: Ring and cancel film (7)

blocks.note: to annul a marriage or law is to cancel it

annotation.surface: Someone phones up and calls off a film.
annotation.walkthrough: Ring looks like a phone call; it is a small circle.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical term in architecture and heraldry, from Latin anulus, a little ring.

entries.clue: Stingy governor in church, economical about energy (12)

indicators.note: in places the governor inside the church letters
about means around, so the word for economical goes round the energy letter

blocks.note: HE = His Excellency, a governor's title

annotation.surface: A mean colonial governor in church is sparing with the heating.
annotation.walkthrough: The energy letter goes in right after the first letter of the economical word, which disguises it well.
annotation.definitionFit: An image made into an adjective: so mean as to pare the rind off cheese.

entries.clue: Silver-haired poet picked up top journalist (10)

indicators.note: a sound picked up is heard, so the poet's name is taken by its sound

blocks.note: Thomas Gray, of the Elegy in a Country Churchyard

annotation.surface: A silver-haired poet is picked up by the chief journalist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top journalist' wants to be one person, the editor, but top and journalist are separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: grey hair and silver hair are the same thing.

entries.clue: Broadcast by artisans dismissing first of such service personnel (11)

indicators.note: to dismiss is to send away, so one letter leaves the word for artisans
the first of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
its first letter, S, is the one removed

annotation.surface: A broadcast by craftsmen dismisses the first of the armed-forces staff.
annotation.walkthrough: The rank is the lowest in the Royal Air Force.
annotation.definitionFit: A rank name: the lowest-ranking members of the RAF, one of the armed services.

entries.clue: Reduce size of quiet skating venue (6)

annotation.surface: A quiet ice rink is being made smaller.
annotation.walkthrough: Quiet is the call for silence, the two letters said to hush a room.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to shrink something is to make it smaller.

entries.clue: Urge to take Liberal inside preserved Arab area (11)

indicators.note: inside means within, so the Liberal letter goes into the word for preserved

annotation.surface: A Liberal feels an urge to take in a protected Arab region.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Urge to take' reads as the start of the wordplay; it is the definition, the compulsion to steal.
annotation.definitionFit: A euphemism: the compulsion is to steal, and take is a polite word for it.

entries.clue: Book miners once found outside a hotel (5)

indicators.note: the miners are found outside, so their letters go round A H

blocks.note: NUM = National Union of Mineworkers, powerful in Britain's coal industry
H = hotel in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Miners of old find a book lying outside a hotel.
annotation.walkthrough: Once points to the union at its height, before the pits closed.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: one of the minor prophets of the Old Testament.

entries.clue: Like some aquatic animals oddly imposing for one I ignored (10)

indicators.note: arranged oddly means put in a strange order, so the letters are shuffled
what is ignored is left out, so one I is dropped from the fodder

blocks.note: a single I is dropped before the shuffle

annotation.surface: Some sea creatures look strangely imposing, though one is ignored.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder has two Is and the answer needs one, which is why 'one I ignored' is there.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: sponges are simple aquatic animals, and -form means shaped like.

entries.clue: Scallywag taking photograph of one applying lash? (14)

annotation.surface: A rascal takes a photo of someone wielding a whip.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the answer as a possessive: the photographer belonging to the person with the lash.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a cheeky, impertinent young person.

entries.clue: Reactive element is a must, somehow, under river (9 (9)

indicators.note: somehow means in some unstated way, so the letters are rearranged
in a down answer, what is under comes after, so the anagram follows the river

blocks.note: a stray copy of the enumeration in the source text

annotation.surface: A reactive chemical is essential, somehow, downstream of a river.
annotation.walkthrough: The Po is the crossword's standard river. The extra '(9' is a typo in the printed text, not part of the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by property: potassium is an alkali metal that reacts violently with water.

entries.clue: Clear first of plants I culled ineptly (8)

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter
done ineptly means done clumsily, so the letters end up out of order

annotation.surface: A gardener clears the first plants but weeds them out clumsily.
annotation.walkthrough: Clear looks like a verb to go with the gardening; it is an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary synonym: pellucid water or prose is transparently clear.

entries.clue: Girl with capacity to contain anger over mischief (9)

indicators.note: to contain is to hold within, so the capacity word holds the anger
turned over means upside down, and in a down answer the anger reads bottom to top

annotation.surface: A capable girl keeps her anger in check despite some mischief.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Anger over' is anger turned upside down in a down clue, not anger finished.
annotation.definitionFit: A French loan: devilry, from diable, devil, so wild mischief.

entries.clue: Copper — married man from Kendal, say (8)

blocks.note: Cu, the chemical symbol for copper

annotation.surface: A married policeman from the town of Kendal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Man from Kendal' wants to be the definition; man is a name, and Kendal is a town in Cumbria, England's Lake District county.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Kendal is one town in the county, hence the 'say'.

entries.clue: Obstruction set back lead communications satellite (7)

indicators.note: something set back is moved backwards, so the obstruction is reversed

blocks.note: let = hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

annotation.surface: A satellite link is held up by an obstruction.
annotation.walkthrough: Let as a noun for obstruction survives in legal phrasing and in tennis.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the satellite launched in 1962 that first relayed live television.

entries.clue: Heavyweight introducing a posh car cover (7)

indicators.note: to introduce is to lead in, so the heavyweight comes first and the rest follows

blocks.note: a metric ton, a heavy weight
U = upper-class, as opposed to non-U

annotation.surface: A heavyweight boxer shows off a posh car cover.
annotation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from Nancy Mitford's essay on U and non-U English.
annotation.definitionFit: A motoring term: a tonneau cover fits over the open back of a car or pickup.

entries.clue: Giant, one primarily attending a fairy queen (7)

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the first letter is taken

annotation.surface: A giant and one attendant wait on a fairy queen.
annotation.walkthrough: The queen is from A Midsummer Night's Dream, wife of Oberon.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Shakespeare's queen of the fairies.

entries.clue: A risk-free time to gather over a woman’s bitter resin (10)

indicators.note: to gather something is to take it in, so the risk-free word takes the over letter inside

annotation.surface: A woman with time to spare collects a bitter resin without risk.
annotation.walkthrough: The link 's is 'is': all the wordplay is the bitter resin.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: a pungent, bitter gum resin used as a spice in Indian cooking.

entries.clue: Boredom initially encompassing Greek character in part of UK (5)

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is taken
in places the Greek letter inside the part of the UK

annotation.surface: Boredom sets in across one part of the UK that has taken in a Greek.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks as if it belongs to Boredom; it picks out the first letter of encompassing, which also looks like a container word.
annotation.definitionFit: A French loan: listless weariness with everything.

entries.clue: Fails with extreme difficulty: a nasty shock! (9)

annotation.surface: Someone fails after a struggle, which comes as a nasty shock.
annotation.walkthrough: In British use to bomb means to fail badly, the opposite of the American 'go down a bomb'.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: news that hits like an exploding shell.

entries.clue: Sergeant major swigging beer in US state capital (5)

indicators.note: to swig a drink is to take it in, so the sergeant major holds the beer inside

annotation.surface: A sergeant major knocks back a beer in an American state capital.
annotation.walkthrough: Most solvers think of the Massachusetts witch trials; the capital is the one in Oregon.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Salem is the capital of Oregon.

entries.clue: Polluted atmosphere originally stifling cat (4)

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, the start, so only the first letter is taken

blocks.note: mog, British slang for a cat

annotation.surface: Polluted air is stifling the family cat.
annotation.walkthrough: Stifling fits the smoky air so well that it looks like part of the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A blend of smoke and fog: air thick with pollution.

entries.clue: Trickster chucks out daughter, one married in Bonn, perhaps (4)

indicators.note: to chuck out is to throw out, so the daughter letter is removed

annotation.surface: A con man in Germany throws out his daughter and marries.
annotation.walkthrough: Bonn signals German, and 'perhaps' that any German-speaking town would do.
annotation.definitionFit: A foreign word: the German for a married woman or wife.

entries.clue: Dancer in male crew carrying flag (6,3)

indicators.note: to carry is to hold, so the male and crew letters hold the flag inside

blocks.note: flag is another name for the iris, and orris is a kind of iris
to crew a ship is to man it

annotation.surface: A dancer joins an all-male crew who carry a flag.
annotation.walkthrough: Flag is the plant, not a banner. The dancer performs the English folk dance with bells and sticks.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a performer of morris dancing, the traditional English folk dance.

entries.clue: Tearjerker holding sanctimonious view (7)

indicators.note: to hold is to have inside, so the tearjerker holds the sanctimonious word

annotation.surface: A weepie film expresses a self-righteous point of view.
annotation.walkthrough: Tearjerker suggests a sad film; it is the vegetable that makes you cry.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what you think on a matter.

entries.clue: Source of beam installed in Agricola’s era (5)

indicators.note: something installed in a place is fitted inside it, so the answer sits inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the end of Agricola's and the start of era

annotation.surface: A roof beam put up in the time of Agricola, Roman governor of Britain.
annotation.walkthrough: Beam suggests a timber in a Roman building; it is a beam of light.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: the device emits a narrow, intense beam of light.

entries.clue: Chap tucking into fleshy fruit is primarily manifesting piggishness (11)

indicators.note: to tuck into is to go inside, so the chap goes into the fruit
primarily means first of all, so only the first letter is taken

blocks.note: a gourd is a large fleshy fruit

annotation.surface: A man tucking into fruit is showing signs of greed.
annotation.walkthrough: Tucking into is the surface's eating and the wordplay's insertion at once.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: greedy love of eating.

entries.clue: Police force info mother receives right by Canadian lake (11)

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it in, so the mother takes the right letter inside
by means next to, so the lake is placed alongside

blocks.note: a dam is an animal's mother
Lake Erie, on the Canada–US border

annotation.surface: The police get information that a mother has been taken in near a Canadian lake.
annotation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information, and mother is the animal sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A French term: the force of gendarmes, France's armed police.
